story:
Earl Fenex sings, and for most of the court that is the whole of what is known about him. He belongs to High Lord Baelerdoth's household in the east, and in the Uncounted Age his work was to sing to his master, because Baelerdoth's thirst never sleeps and Fenex's voice was the one thing near him it could not drink. A ward goes thin in that hall, and a demon's strength goes thin, but a song is not held by anyone, and so it cannot be taken. Baelerdoth slept for the first time to Fenex singing, and has slept to nothing else since.

He is a creature of fire, like the firebird of the old bestiaries, and in the early Rolls he sang beside the braziers that Duke Harboris fed from the deep cracks with the fire in his ribs. When Harboris climbed toward the world in the Eighth Roll and came back a ghost with no fire in him, the braziers of Baelerdoth's hall went out. The court expected the high lord to wake and stay awake. Fenex kept him sleeping by setting himself in the cold braziers and burning there, and singing while he burned, and he has done it every Roll since. Each time he burns a little lower and comes back out of the ash a little smaller. His shape is a duke's and his line an earl's, and the imps say it is the duke's shape that is burning away.

What Fenex wants is Harboris's line. It reads Keeper of the Fires, and Harboris keeps it though he has lit nothing since his climb. Fenex walked down the approach in the Ninth Roll to ask the Chancellor for it, and Adremal answered that the bargain does not require a keeper of fires to keep any, as it does not require a marquis to be alive or a duke to have a body. Fenex went back east and sang the answer to Baelerdoth, set to a tune. The court considers it the only joke ever made against the Chancellor that he has not answered. The ghost duke stands a short walk from the singing and does not seem to hear it.
legend: Fenex stands in High Lord Baelerdoth's hall in the east, between Duke Harboris and the high lord himself, both within about seven hundred units. That is the whole problem: pull Fenex badly and you have the ghost duke, the high lord, or both. Level 71, no script, duke-sized for an earl. Take Harboris first, then Fenex, then Focalleste, and only then Baelerdoth, and keep every fight out toward the Ward. Players call him the singer and swear you can hear him singing if the hall is quiet, and some say Baelerdoth sleeps until Fenex dies. That part is not true, but it is still a good reason to leave Fenex until just before the high lord and have every buff fresh when he drops.

Burn quietly. He hates to be woken.

loremasterTopic.text: Earl of High Lord [Baelerdoth]'s household, the singer whose voice is the one thing his master's thirst cannot drink. Since Duke [Harboris] came back a ghost, Fenex burns in the cold braziers to keep the hall lit, and he wants the line of Keeper of the Fires.

bookPage: From a song of the College of Bards at Tir na Nog, The Singer in the Ash, set down in prose: There is a hall in the east of the pit where the fires went out, and the lord there sleeps. Beside him a singer stands in a cold brazier and sets himself alight and sings, so that the lord will not wake. We heard him from the foot of the eastern stair. Our own bard put down her harp and listened, and afterwards she would not play for three nights. When she played again it was his tune, and she said it was the saddest thing she had ever learned: a song for keeping someone asleep.
